newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila mills reject 70,000T U.S., Canadian wheat.
newsitem.headline: Manila mills reject 70,000T U.S., Canadian wheat.

text.p: Four Philippine flour millers have rejected offers for the supply of 70,000 tonnes of Canadian and U.S. wheat due to high prices, traders said on Wednesday.
The firms solicited tenders for the supply of the wheat for April and May shipments late on Tuesday, they said.
"We rejected all offers due to high prices. We got offers of $195 per tonne FOB for U.S. wheat and $190 per tonne for Canadian wheat," an executive in one of the firms told Reuters.
"We believed that prices are artificially being raised by speculators and it's not proper for wheat importers like the Philippines to be sucked up by this market," the executive added.
The four Philippine millers can afford to stay on the sidelines and wait for prices to soften due to ample supply, the executive said.
